analysis: Examined three files. (1) WholeMacServiceBudget.swift adds isIdle(for:), performIfIdle(for:_:) and isIdleLocked (lines ~233-252). These are lock-held idle checks based on charges, unboundedActivities and idleSince. They do not touch the A-001 plaintext path, the A-016 authorization, or any provider/coordinator wire contract. performIfIdle runs the body under NSLock, and the documented contract forbids reentry. A reentrant caller would deadlock, which is an availability risk, but no caller is in the supplied evidence, so this is unverified and not a finding. The body is non-escaping, and NSLock is non-recursive. (2) ProviderLoop+NemotronSuperAdmission.swift changes the memory-admission logic. evictUntilNemotronSuperFits now calls releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad() once (guarded by the poolDropped flag) before evicting idle models. nemotronSuperLoadIsCertainToFail becomes async and gains the helper nemotronSuperRoomReaches. Eviction is bounded by the declined-eviction limit, and the one-shot poolDropped flag prevents a release loop. The release functions and reclaimableMemoryBytes(from:countingRetainedKVSegments:) are outside the supplied evidence. Their behavior on retained KV segments, possibly including prefix-cache state (T-041, T-028), is unverified. The async conversion introduces suspension points, so callers must re-check state after the await (the doc comment says so), and the callers are not supplied. The change appears to affect only availability and resource management. It does not change the cache's encryption, scope, TTL or storage, so T-041 and T-028 are not materially affected. Releasing retained segments reduces residual memory. (3) ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift is a comment-only change. Remaining integration questions: the implementation of releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad, the windowed proactiveReclaimSweep, the callers of nemotronSuperLoadIsCertainToFail, and whether performIfIdle is used with a body that reenters the budget. No concrete security regression was identified in the supplied code.
